items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: [(note)] Joe was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 11, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

ctx.x: Joe Temperley was born in Cowdenbealth, Scotland in 1929. Jazz became his passion and he took advantage of the playing opportunities available in Scotland and England, including a lengthy stint with the Humphrey-Lyttelton Band. He immigrated to the U.S. in 1965 and found a niche for his distinctive baritone sax in the bands of Woody Herman, Buddy Rich, Thad Jones-Mel Lewis and on numerous recordings. Joe was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 11, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Aspen, Colorado. It’s my pleasure to be talking with Joe Temperley today, saxophonist, baritonist, and sopranoist and all the other ists. Bass clarinetist. We were just talking about the hazards — not hazards — but things you have to deal with being on the road and traveling in planes. Does that get tiring?
